terra.problem: The passage does not identify any priests or Levites on the guest list, but it does not establish that none were among the Rechabites.
Calling the baker's choice a funny pick makes the answer itself the joke.
Jonadab forbade building houses, not all buildings or living in towns. The passage also does not say their stay in Jerusalem was a visit rather than a plan to settle.
The chocolate-chip comparison is unclear: it is hard to picture what getting chips past a batch means or how it relates to keeping a rule.
Saying the Rechabites wanted walls adds a reason the passage does not give. They say they went to Jerusalem to escape the armies.
The passage does not say Jonadab forbade buying land or owning fields. It says he forbade building houses, sowing seed and planting vineyards, and that the Rechabites had not owned fields.
The explanation says the text does not call the rules too hard, then states as fact that they were hard.
The passage says the Rechabites carried out Jonadab's commands, not that they remembered every word.
The passage does not say whether the people found the message confusing. The explanation rules that out as a reason without support.
The explanation repeats the warning in generic terms without adding much explanation or Papa Dorin's personality.
The spelling comparison and the line about handling a king are unclear and do not help explain the answer.
Saying he will not joke about the line comments on how he tells the passage.
Jonadab did not say his descendants would never own fields or vineyards. He forbade planting a vineyard; the Rechabites say they had not owned vineyards or fields.
Calling the baker's choice a funny pick makes the answer itself the joke.
Calling standing before God a different job adds a role the passage does not specify.
